answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it may influence a reputation-weighted market. When an identity is caught coordinating fraud, peers submit signed evidence and a challenge bond; an adjudicator checks the receipts, then burns part of the deposit and rewards the challenger. Creating a canyon of fake accounts therefore requires capital for every account, while getting caught destroys that capital. A quill or a fable may make identities look distinct, but neither replaces the costly bond.
